strings.A box channel or rectangular hollow sect: A box channel or rectangular hollow section is a rectangle with a rectangular void inside. This calculator uses the cross-section area B × H − (B − 2T) × (H − 2T), multiplies it by the length and by the material density, so the answer is the mass of the steel walls only.

strings.A hot-rolled round bar is normally suppl: A hot-rolled round bar is normally supplied slightly over the nominal diameter, and a broached hexagon can be a little under size. Those tolerances move the real weight by a few percent either way.
strings.A flanged flat head is a flat crown bent: A flanged flat head is a flat crown bent down into a straight flange through a corner radius R. The crown stays at the level of the top of that bend, so its height above the tangent line where the knuckle turns vertical equals the knuckle radius. The flat crown diameter is then ID − 2R.
strings.A full-thread bolt uses the physical thr: A full-thread bolt uses the physical thread approximation for its whole length. A half-thread bolt uses the solid shank cylinder for the unthreaded portion and the thread approximation only over the entered thread length.
strings.A circle fills only π ÷ 4, about 78.5%,: A circle fills only π ÷ 4, about 78.5%, of the square that encloses it. A 500 mm disc therefore weighs roughly three quarters of a 500 × 500 mm plate of the same thickness.
strings.A hexagon fills 86.6% of the square that: A hexagon fills 86.6% of the square that encloses it, so a 40 mm hex bar weighs about 10.88 kg/m against 12.56 kg/m for a 40 mm square bar.
strings.A is the distance across flats of the re: A is the distance across flats of the regular hexagon, L is bar length, and ρ is material density.
strings.A regular hexagon with across-flats size: A regular hexagon with across-flats size A has an area of (√3 ÷ 2) × A². Multiply that by the length and the density to get the mass, which is the formula used in this calculator.
strings.A round plate is a cylinder of thickness: A round plate is a cylinder of thickness T. This calculator uses (π ÷ 4) × D² × T for the volume, multiplies by the density and divides by 10⁶ when dimensions are in millimetres, so you get kilograms directly.
strings.A is the width and B is the height of th: A is the width and B is the height of the solid cross-section, L is length, and ρ is material density.
strings.A sphere has volume (4 ÷ 3) × π × r³, wh: A sphere has volume (4 ÷ 3) × π × r³, where r is half the diameter. Multiply that by the density, and for dimensions in millimetres divide by 1,000,000 to get kilograms.
strings.A is the outer regular hexagon across-fl: A is the outer regular hexagon across-flats dimension, d is the concentric round hole diameter, L is length, and ρ is density. Hole must fit inside the hexagon.
strings.A tee is one flange plate plus one web p: A tee is one flange plate plus one web plate: B × T
strings.A thread has crests and roots, so a soli: A thread has crests and roots, so a solid cylinder overstates its metal area. The calculator uses a geometric approximation: the mean of the major-diameter circle and the basic root-diameter circle of the 60° thread. The tensile stress area is a strength-design value and is not used for mass.
strings.A square of side D has 4 ÷ π, about 1.27: A square of side D has 4 ÷ π, about 1.27 times the area of a circle of diameter D. A 25 mm square bar therefore weighs 4.91 kg/m against 3.85 kg/m for a 25 mm round bar.
strings.A square of side D fills 4 ÷ π times the: A square of side D fills 4 ÷ π times the area of a circle of diameter D. A 25 mm square bar weighs 4.91 kg/m while a 25 mm round bar weighs 3.85 kg/m.
strings.A typical DN100 PN16 flange has a 220 mm: A typical DN100 PN16 flange has a 220 mm outside diameter, a 115 mm bore, about 20 mm thickness and eight 18 mm bolt holes on a 180 mm PCD. That plate weighs roughly 4.02 kg in carbon steel; the hub and raised face of a weld-neck flange are extra.

strings.About 0.51 kg in mild steel. The volume: About 0.51 kg in mild steel. The volume falls with the cube of the diameter, so halving the size reduces the weight to one eighth.
strings.About 2.47 kg/m in mild steel, because t: About 2.47 kg/m in mild steel, because the area is 314.2 mm². This is the familiar shortcut D² ÷ 162 for steel bars in millimetres.
strings.About 0.89 kg/m in steel. The same calcu: About 0.89 kg/m in steel. The same calculation covers 8 mm (0.40 kg/m) and 16 mm (1.58 kg/m) bars, which is why the D² shortcut is used on site.
strings.About 233.7 kg, using 1220 × 2440 mm. If: About 233.7 kg, using 1220 × 2440 mm. If your supplier cuts 1250 × 2500 mm instead, the same thickness weighs 245.3 kg, so confirm the actual sheet size before ordering.
strings.About 3.14 kg/m in mild steel, since the: About 3.14 kg/m in mild steel, since the area is 400 mm². The shop shortcut is A² ÷ 127, which gives the same result for steel.
strings.About 2.72 kg/m in mild steel, because t: About 2.72 kg/m in mild steel, because the area is (√3 ÷ 2) × 400 = 346.4 mm². This is the value behind the common shortcut A² × 0.0068 for steel.
strings.About 245.3 kg in mild steel. This is a: About 245.3 kg in mild steel. This is a standard 8 × 4 ft sheet size, which covers 3.125 m² and therefore weighs 3.125 × 78.5 kg.
strings.About 28.7 kg/m in mild steel. A 6 m she: About 28.7 kg/m in mild steel. A 6 m shell course of the same size is roughly 172 kg.
strings.About 4.44 kg in mild steel. Halving the: About 4.44 kg in mild steel. Halving the diameter to 300 mm and reducing the thickness to 8 mm removes most of the volume compared with a 500 × 10 mm disc.
strings.Across-flats is the distance between two: Across-flats is the distance between two opposite flat faces, which is how hex bar is ordered and how a spanner grips a nut. It is not the distance between opposite corners, which is larger by a factor of 1.155.

strings.Surface area of the semi-ellipsoid (a >: Surface area of the semi-ellipsoid (a > b, e = √(1 − b² ÷ a²)): A = πa² + (πb² ÷ 2e) × ln((1 + e) ÷ (1 − e)); for b > a the asin form is used.
strings.The calculator works on the inside surfa: The calculator works on the inside surface, matching the inside diameter you enter. Using outside dimensions would raise the area by roughly 2T/R, which is small beside forming and mill tolerances for normal plate thicknesses.
strings.The circumference is divided into the se: The circumference is divided into the selected number of equal angular divisions (12 to 96); each station is reported with its plan radius, height, meridian length and blank coordinates.
strings.The crown and the knuckle together have: The crown and the knuckle together have more surface than a flat disc of the same diameter, so the area-equivalent blank 2 × √(A ÷ π) is larger than ID. A production blank also needs a forming and trim allowance on top of that.
strings.The crown is spherical with radius C.R a: The crown is spherical with radius C.R and the knuckle is a torus of radius K.R. Where the two meet, the height above the tangent line is H = C.R − √((C.R − K.R)² − (R − K.R)²) with R = ID ÷ 2. The height is therefore calculated from the diameter and the two radii, not entered.
strings.The crown is the spherical zone of radiu: The crown is the spherical zone of radius C.R above the tangent point: A = 2π × C.R × (H − K.R × sin θk). Only the part of the sphere above the knuckle is counted, so the crown area falls as the knuckle grows.
strings.The developed blank is the area-equivale: The developed blank is the area-equivalent flat plate: Ø = 2 × √(A ÷ π).
strings.The dish is a true semi-ellipsoid with a: The dish is a true semi-ellipsoid with a = ID ÷ 2 and b = H, so a 2:1 head is H = ID ÷ 4.
strings.The dish is half an ellipsoid of revolut: The dish is half an ellipsoid of revolution with semi-axes a = ID ÷ 2 and b = H. With e = √(1 − b² ÷ a²) the area is πa² + (πb² ÷ 2e) × ln((1 + e) ÷ (1 − e)); when the head is taller than it is wide (b > a) the same integral is evaluated with the inverse-sine form.
strings.The dome is half a sphere with area 2πR²: The dome is half a sphere with area 2πR², and the straight flange adds 2π × R × SF. Multiplying the total area by the plate thickness and the density gives the weight; at ID 1000 mm the dome alone is 1.571 m².
strings.The height is the vertical semi-axis of: The height is the vertical semi-axis of the ellipsoid. A flatter dish (smaller H) has less surface for the same diameter, so the area, blank diameter and weight all fall; as H approaches ID ÷ 2 the area approaches the hemispherical 2πR².
strings.The knuckle is a torus swept about the h: The knuckle is a torus swept about the head axis: A = 2π × K.R × [(R − K.R) × θk + K.R × sin θk], where θk is the knuckle arc angle in radians. The arc runs from the tangent point to the start of the vertical flange.
strings.The knuckle radius R is the corner radiu: The knuckle radius R is the corner radius between the flat crown and the straight flange; the crown diameter is ID − 2R and the crown sits R above the tangent line.
strings.The meridian is a quarter ellipse; the t: The meridian is a quarter ellipse; the true length from the apex to a station is integrated from s(t) = ∫₀ᵗ √(R²cos²u + H²sin²u) du.
strings.They divide the circumference into 12 to: They divide the circumference into 12 to 96 equal angular steps and control the station table and the radial lines drawn on the section and the blank. More divisions give a finer template; the area, blank diameter and weight do not change.
